canonicalExplanation.summary: Links that leave your site or download a file should **set expectations**: say in the link text (or a visible note) that it's an external site, a PDF, or a download, and how big. Don't force new tabs by default — users can choose. When you truly need `target="_blank"`, modern browsers imply `rel="noopener"`, but adding `rel="noopener noreferrer"` makes the intent explicit and protects older browsers.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner clicks "Docs" and suddenly lands on another website in a new tab, with no way back via the Back button. Another clicks "Syllabus" and a 20 MB PDF starts downloading on mobile data. Neither link warned them. A link identifies that documentation opens on an external site and avoids forcing a new context unless the product requires it. In this lesson you'll configure an external or downloadable link without opener or expectation surprises.

```predict
{"question": "Should every external link open in a new tab?", "options": ["Yes, always safer", "No — let users decide; new tabs break Back and can disorient screen-reader users"], "answer": 1, "why": "Users can open any link in a new tab themselves. Forcing it removes that choice and breaks the Back button."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Sections and landmarks**, **Files, folders and paths**, and **Meaningful links**.

sections.heading: The model: tell users before they click
sections.body: ```html MDN Web Docs (external site) Download the syllabus (PDF, 2 MB) Payment help (opens in a new tab) ``` | Situation | Do | |---|---| | external site. | say so in the text or with a labelled icon. | | file download. | give type and size; `download` attribute if appropriate. | | forced new tab. | only with a reason; say "opens in a new tab"; add rel="noopener". | ```reveal {"prompt": "What risk does `rel=\"noopener\"` prevent?", "answer": "Without it, a page opened with target=_blank could use `window.opener` to redirect your original tab to a fake login page (\"tabnabbing\")."} ```

sections.heading: Name the surprise

includes: Label external links, downloads, file types and sizes.
Use target=_blank only when justified, with rel="noopener noreferrer" and a visible note.

outcomes: Configure an external or downloadable link without opener or expectation surprises.

examples.title: Linking to outside documentation
examples.situation: A link identifies that documentation opens on an external site and avoids forcing a new context unless the product requires it.
walkthrough: **Identify:** the link text reads "MDN Web Docs (external site)", so users know it leaves the course.
**Avoid forcing a new context:** no target=_blank, so Back returns to the lesson and users choose tabs themselves.
**Exception:** on the payment form, where leaving would lose input, the help link will open in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer" and says so.
examples.result: Users know where each link goes and keep control of tabs, except where the product genuinely requires a new context.

examples.title: The silent download
examples.situation: A lesson page links "Slides" to a 45 MB .pptx file.
walkthrough: Mobile users unknowingly spend data and may not be able to open .pptx.
Fix: "Download slides (PowerPoint, 45 MB)" and offer a lighter HTML or PDF version.
examples.result: Users can decide whether and how to download before clicking.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Every external link must open a new tab because that is always safer and more accessible.
misconceptions.correction: Forced new tabs remove user choice, break the Back button and can confuse assistive technology users. Keep the same tab by default, clearly label external links and downloads, and open new tabs only when there's a real need, with rel="noopener".
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Linking to outside documentation", when is a new tab justified?

analogy.example: External links are like **doors in a building**: a sign saying "Exit to street" or "Storage room — heavy boxes" lets people choose. Forcing a new tab is like a door that teleports you to a new building while your original one stays open behind you.
usefulFor: remembering to label where a link leads
limitations: Doors don't have security risks like window.opener.
Users can "open in new tab" themselves; they can't choose to un-teleport.

nearTransfer.prompt: Rewrite: `here` for a page where leaving is fine.

farTransfer.prompt: Audit all external links and downloads on a site you built. Label each, remove unjustified target=_blank, and add rel and a visible note where a new tab remains.
expectedEvidence: Every external link and download clearly labelled.
Remaining new-tab links justified with rel and notes.

remediation.explanation: For each link ask: **Does it leave the site? Download a file? Open a new tab?** Each yes must be visible in the link text — and the new tab must have a reason.

recap.summary: To configure an external or downloadable link without surprises, label external destinations, file types and sizes in the link text, keep the same tab by default, and use target=_blank only when needed — with rel="noopener noreferrer" and a visible note.
